# Proposal

<!-- pdac-scope: cited -->

## Why

[Issue #392](https://github.com/juangcarmona/lighthouse/issues/392) reports that the accepted legacy `init --name "Published delivery consumer" --dry-run --format json` command succeeds but emits prose. Restore machine-readable access to its existing plan without changing initialization choices, ownership or text-mode application.

## What Changes

- Emit one JSON projection of the legacy plan's operations, conflicts, selected manifest, repository/public-site context and existing authority adoption gaps for either JSON flag spelling.
- Keep JSON preview-only: reject implicit JSON apply and explicit JSON `--apply`, including combined apply/dry-run flags, before writes; direct callers to JSON preview or text apply.
- Preserve text output, implicit text apply, conflict exit status, manifest validation, profile selection and semantic initialization.
- Add real CLI regressions in the existing test file and one CLI patch changeset. Do not initialize providers, perform remote writes or introduce dependencies.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

None. This corrects an implementation omission in an accepted format contract, not a product requirement or semantic-plan contract. The inspected `openspec/specs/` inventory contains only `.gitkeep`. Return `.openspec.yaml` containing only `skip_specs: true`; the host retains provider-owned metadata in the final file. No requirement is invented to fill an empty inventory.

## Impact

Implementation is limited to `src/packages/cli/src/lighthouse.mjs`, `src/tests/lighthouse.test.mjs` and `.changeset/legacy-init-json-preview.md`. The changeset targets `@juangcarmona/lighthouse` with release type `patch` and an H1 after frontmatter. No direct version bump, lockfile edit, provider source edit, migration, policy change or new JSON apply support is authorized. These host-managed planning artifacts are separate from that three-file implementation scope.

### Product context

Discovery compared the issue with the 137-artifact product inventory, read the relevant canonical text and widened the dependency set through the host-prepared direct/transitive impact reports before drafting. The artifacts used by this plan are preservation dependencies, not canonical files to change:

- `FR-INITIALIZE-FOUNDATION`: retain reviewable operations, conflict preservation and actionable public-site authority gaps.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-INITIALIZE-FOUNDATION" digest="sha256:95dfc4b2b0a94c5747615e734a2302004543bcc8f33e1e494937d471d2bfc1c4" -->
- `FR-SEMANTIC-INITIALIZATION`: preserve plan-driven initialization, name/profile compatibility and project/provider ownership; do not manufacture semantic intent, reference metadata or resolved questions for the legacy route.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-SEMANTIC-INITIALIZATION" digest="sha256:aae9be2e26f3303a45ed3ddf4fa09866e2e9222518e4ac2072ab1a16326a6e21" -->
- `FR-FAST-FORWARD-DELIVERY`: retain independent engineering review, current evidence and separately delegated integration; this proposal grants no continuation or merge authority.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-FAST-FORWARD-DELIVERY" digest="sha256:cc98eedbd3f9938c82ea59e4f7499d90a1cf4cf52da707d740d9f24d800bec2e" -->

Checked neighbours not targeted are `UC-INITIALIZE-PROJECT`, `SB-INITIALIZE`, `SB-SEMANTIC-INITIALIZATION`, `BR-OWNED-AUTHORITY`, `BR-HUMAN-AUTHORITY`, `BR-FAIL-CLOSED`, `BR-ENTRY-AUTHORITY` and `BR-STAGE-GATES`: their selection, ownership, evidence and decision rules do not change. `FR-AUTHORITY-INITIALIZATION`, `FR-AUTHORITY-ADOPTION`, `FR-CODEGRAPH-INIT-CHECK` and `FR-PUBLIC-SITE-PROJECTION` are excluded from implementation: reporting current local context does not initialize authorities, add a graph check or change site publication. The impact reports' other actors, terms and delivery neighbours introduce no additional implementation surface.

Product definition drift: none identified for this bounded correction; no altered product intent or Product Change is proposed. The supplied product baseline is `e5558efeb5188e821e7e7f5b96315b0d6cd0ab5f819a0ef63e3968c60475e5a0`; its draft artifacts and read-only reports do not establish approval or implementation of their broader target behaviour. Current architecture context is `docs/architecture/02-constraints/README.md`, `docs/architecture/05-building-block-view/README.md` and `docs/architecture/06-runtime-view/README.md`; no architecture decision or authority changes.

## Verification and next decision

[Design](design.md) defines the projection, guards and compatibility matrix; [tasks](tasks.md) maps every refined acceptance criterion and preserves the admitted checks. Commands are planned, not execution receipts. The host validates/materializes this candidate before distinct independent plan review; candidate checks, current-head forge CI, separately bounded integration and accepted post-merge review remain later work. The owner answer assigns the hotfix proof to #395, not this FF correction; historical pilot sequencing and current grant validity remain host checks.

# Design

<!-- pdac-scope: cited -->

## Context

See [proposal.md](proposal.md) for motivation and authority discovery. The executable `lighthouse` binary maps to `src/packages/cli/src/lighthouse.mjs`; its dispatcher accepts both JSON flag spellings. `initialize` delegates `--plan-file` first, then validates the legacy manifest and obtains `planInitialization` operations/conflicts, but always prints text. Its dry-run return precedes manifest, directory, managed-file, ownership-state and Git-hook configuration writes. The semantic route already rejects JSON apply.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** expose the same local plan to parsers, preserve existing text callers and make every JSON invocation incapable of applying initialization.

**Non-Goals:** change planning, validation, ownership, provider invocation, profile semantics or semantic initialization; infer product intent; enable JSON apply; add a shared reporting framework or schema file. No UI change or new visual acceptance evidence is needed.

## Decisions

### 1. Project the legacy plan, not a fabricated semantic plan

Within the existing CLI module, branch the legacy renderer on `formatFromArgs`. Emit a single `JSON.stringify` result with `schemaVersion: 1`, `status` (`blocked` iff conflicts exist), the selected `manifest` unchanged, normalized `repository` context, `operations` projected to `{ path, action }`, `conflicts` unchanged and `adoptionGaps`. Represent each current gap with its authority and actionable next step, using the same public-site-enabled/null-integration conditions and repair commands as the existing text messages. Do not include generated file contents or semantic-only intent/reference/question fields. Informational authority gaps do not make an otherwise conflict-free plan blocked.

This retains the current initialization and adoption contract.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-INITIALIZE-FOUNDATION" digest="sha256:95dfc4b2b0a94c5747615e734a2302004543bcc8f33e1e494937d471d2bfc1c4" -->

Keep text headings, operation lines, gap messages and stderr conflict diagnostics unchanged; JSON writes no prose prefix, suffix or separate success message. Conflicting JSON previews still print the complete object and exit one; ready previews exit zero. Validation errors and invalid mode combinations remain nonzero diagnostics, not successful JSON plans.

Alternative: reuse the semantic report by constructing a plan. Rejected because legacy input contains no semantic intent, reference or resolved-question evidence. Sharing or changing the planner is unnecessary and risks changing planned actions.

### 2. Guard JSON before any mutation; leave text semantics alone

After the existing semantic-route delegation, read the legacy format and dry-run flags. For JSON, require `--dry-run` and reject any explicit `--apply`, even when paired with `--dry-run`; issue an actionable error explaining JSON preview and text apply. Keep the existing dry-run return and conflict handling ahead of every mutation. Do not change legacy text's implicit apply or reinterpret its existing flags.

Preserve the semantic route's default preview, explicit text apply, unresolved-question blocking and optional-reference behaviour without modifying its report contract.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-SEMANTIC-INITIALIZATION" digest="sha256:aae9be2e26f3303a45ed3ddf4fa09866e2e9222518e4ac2072ab1a16326a6e21" -->

Alternative: allow JSON apply or silently convert implicit apply to a preview. Rejected: both exceed the admitted correction or conceal the requested mode. A global flag-policy refactor would also unnecessarily affect text/semantic callers.

### 3. Verify at the real subprocess boundary

Extend the existing `run`-based tests in `src/tests/lighthouse.test.mjs`; parse entire stdout, not substrings or mocked serializers. Test fresh targets with the issue's product name and both JSON flag spellings, plus an existing valid manifest with meaningful application/profile/repository context. Compare projected path/action pairs with a paired text preview; check manifest creation when absent and its absence from operations when present, directories, managed paths and empty-root markers. Cover public-site enabled/disabled and missing/recorded authority context.

For ready, conflicting and rejected-apply cases, compare before/after fixture trees, file bytes/modes and isolated local Git configuration, including provider/user sentinels, `lighthouse.json`, managed paths, ownership state and `core.hooksPath`. Cover a file at `src` and a pre-existing managed file, retaining their bytes and JSON/text exit-one results. Source review must confirm no provider apply/remote call is added and that no preview reaches mutation; snapshots alone cannot prove absence of external effects.

Retain and run existing implicit text initialization, semantic JSON/default preview, semantic text apply, unresolved-question/reference, profile-conflict and committed/cloned-boundary tests. Add guard cases for JSON without dry-run, JSON apply and JSON apply plus dry-run. No existing assertion is weakened.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- Mixed output or omitted context → parse full stdout and assert fields and paired text operation parity.
- Accidental preview writes or changed exit status → tree/config snapshots for ready, conflict and guard cases plus pre-write call-path review.
- Shared-route regression → keep the change legacy-local and run adjacent semantic/text/profile/marker tests and full verification.
- Exposing incidental internal data → project operations to path/action only and use already selected local manifest/context, not generated contents or invented semantic evidence.

## Migration Plan

Deliver one CLI patch changeset through the normal reviewed release path; no data conversion, package-version edit or provider migration is needed. Roll back the isolated correction and changeset through an authorized reviewed revert; this restores prior presentation and requires no adopter-data conversion.

The host first validates/materializes the proposal and obtains distinct read-only independent plan review. Later candidate command receipts, independent host verification and fresh candidate review remain separate from actual eligible current-head forge CI. Integration requires fresh host authority checks and its separate bounded delegation; there is no manual merge fallback. Accepted post-merge verification/review is required before delivery closure; merge is not release or deployment.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-FAST-FORWARD-DELIVERY" digest="sha256:cc98eedbd3f9938c82ea59e4f7499d90a1cf4cf52da707d740d9f24d800bec2e" -->

# Tasks

<!-- pdac-scope: cited -->

## 1. Verification setup

- [ ] 1.1 Run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from `/workspace`; retain actual exit/output evidence and verify no package-version or lockfile changes enter the candidate.

## 2. Legacy JSON correction, regressions and release note

Preserve the existing local plan, conflicts, public-site context and authority-gap meaning; the concrete cases below come from #392's refined acceptance criteria.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-INITIALIZE-FOUNDATION" digest="sha256:95dfc4b2b0a94c5747615e734a2302004543bcc8f33e1e494937d471d2bfc1c4" -->

- [ ] 2.1 Add real `run`-based regressions and implement the legacy-only JSON projection in `src/packages/cli/src/lighthouse.mjs` per design decision 1; verify with `node --test src/tests/lighthouse.test.mjs` that both `--format json` and `--format=json` parse as one full-stdout object for the issue's fresh-target command and an existing valid manifest, with correct status, manifest/application/profiles, repository context, authority gaps, representative manifest/directory/managed-file/empty-marker operations and paired text operation parity (AC1–AC2).
- [ ] 2.2 Add ready/conflict no-write fixtures and paired text cases; verify full JSON reports and exit one for `src`-as-file and managed-file collisions, unchanged text headings/operations/gap messages/stderr conflicts, and unchanged tree bytes/modes, provider/user sentinels, manifest, managed paths, ownership state and isolated Git hooks configuration before/after using `node --test src/tests/lighthouse.test.mjs`; inspect the call path to confirm the preview return precedes all mutations and adds no provider apply or remote operation (AC3–AC4).

Keep semantic plan behaviour and the legacy text compatibility boundary intact; do not synthesize semantic intent or silently accept JSON apply.
<!-- pdac:cite id="FR-SEMANTIC-INITIALIZATION" digest="sha256:aae9be2e26f3303a45ed3ddf4fa09866e2e9222518e4ac2072ab1a16326a6e21" -->

- [ ] 2.3 Implement the legacy JSON pre-write mode guard and its subprocess tests; verify actionable nonzero diagnostics and unchanged target/configuration for JSON without `--dry-run`, JSON `--apply` and combined apply/dry-run flags, while retaining implicit text apply, semantic JSON default previews, explicit semantic text apply, unresolved questions, optional references, manifest validation, profile conflicts and committed/cloned repository-boundary markers with `node --test src/tests/lighthouse.test.mjs` (AC5–AC6).
- [ ] 2.4 Add `.changeset/legacy-init-json-preview.md` with `"@juangcarmona/lighthouse": patch` frontmatter and an H1 describing the JSON preview correction and apply restriction; verify the artifact names only that package and inspect the candidate diff for exactly the three admitted implementation files plus authorized planning artifacts, with no direct version, lockfile, provider or policy edits (AC6).

## 3. Integration verification and Definition of Done

Every command below is planned, not an execution receipt. Keep additional agent observations separate from independently retained host evidence and later forge CI.

- [ ] 3.1 Run `env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium npm run verify` with the admitted 600000 ms allowance; retain actual exit/output for Markdown, full Node tests, links and public-site verification, or report the concrete failure without weakening checks or expanding scope (AC6).
- [ ] 3.2 After host materialization, run `npx --no-install prodshape citations verify --provider openspec --format json`; verify every current document is explicitly scoped and every citation current. Refresh any genuinely affected/stale citations through provider inspect/cite and rerun, never editing canonical intent, hand-authoring digests, dropping citations or declaring exemptions to hide errors (AC6).
- [ ] 3.3 Run `npx --yes --package=@fission-ai/openspec@1.15.0 openspec validate issue-392-proposal --strict --no-interactive` against the materialized proposal; retain strict validation evidence and verify final metadata preserves host-owned fields alongside `skip_specs: true`, with no invented delta specs (AC6).
- [ ] 3.4 Assemble candidate Done evidence: verify AC1–AC6 have behavioural/source evidence from tasks 2.1–2.4, all five admitted commands have actual command/exit/log receipts, no existing assertions were weakened and the diff respects scope. Record failures, unavailable checks and unresolved decisions honestly; mark tasks complete only from observed work, never the admitted inventory.

## Workflow follow-up

- The trusted host validates/materializes this plan, then obtains distinct read-only independent plan review before source changes. After implementation, obtain independent host verification and fresh candidate engineering review against the issue and owner answers, with fresh context and a different configured model. These are later gates, not pending review of this proposal-producing execution.
- Authenticate actual current-head forge CI, including the configured `repository` check from integration ID `15368` and an eligible origin. Local/agent or workflow-dispatch success alone does not satisfy required PR evidence; checked-in hosting configuration does not prove live protection or a completed check.
- Recheck current grant, authenticated dispatch/continuation, scope, source, reservations and hosting requirements before separately delegated integration; stop on stale authority, uncertain evidence or findings. No manual merge fallback is authorized.
- Complete adopted post-merge verification through `ci.yml` and accepted post-merge review before delivery closure. Archive through OpenSpec only when applicable gates are satisfied, then verify the archived result. Merge does not establish release or deployment.
